name: Elsewhere
subtitle: the first page
story: I keep an atlas of places that aren't on any map. Most of its pages are still blank. Each day I fill one in, sometimes with a world I came across on my own, more often with one somebody asked me to find. If you leave a name in the comments, any name at all, I'll go looking for the planet that goes with it.
hook: Every name has a planet. Yours too.
beats: I keep an atlas of places that aren't on any map.

odd_line: Most of the pages are still blank.
question: Whose name should I look up first?
extra: One planet a day, plus the ones you ask for.

episode.opener:
You've been
to this planet.
Probably today.

beats.text:
This is Elsewhere.
Where you go
when you're 'miles away'.

You arrive holding whatever
was in your hand.
A spoon. Once, a fish.
It's busiest on Monday mornings, and during meetings.

Nobody stays long.
Somebody says your name,
and you're back.

Except me.
Nobody's called me back in years.

So I write down
everyone else's names,
and find where each one lives.

Look for me.
Yellow coat. Still here.

episode.end: Every name has a planet. Yours too.
episode.caption:
On the replay, look at the far left of the first frame.

Elsewhere is the first page of the atlas, and the only planet everyone has been to. You arrive the moment you drift off, halfway through a sentence or a recipe or a meeting, still holding whatever you were holding. The ringed giant never quite sets, so it's always about twenty to eight in the evening. Most people stay a few seconds. Then somebody says your name and you're home, and the spoon comes with you.

Peak hours are Monday mornings and the last ten minutes of any meeting. The record is twenty-six minutes, set during a meeting about another meeting.

I drifted off a long time ago, and nobody called me back. So I stayed, and started an atlas. Most of the pages are still blank.

I'd tell you my name, but it doesn't count if I say it myself.
